messages:
incident_bot: INCIDENT ALERT — streaming-pipeline p99 spike detected in prod-us-west-2. Rule: streaming_latency.p99 > 1200ms for 3m. Link: https://alerts.redwood/status/streams/alert/4871 :rotating_light:

oncall_alex: on it, paging. grabbing logs and routing table.

duty_lead_maya: are we seeing customer errors or just elevated latency? any 5xx counts?

customer_success_raj: customer-reports channel: two customers (enterprise-acct-01, vendor-x) reported timeouts while generating long chat responses (~30s). CS pinged them and asked for request ids.

ml_ops_jess: looking at model-serving dashboard -> per-route p95/p99: p95 from 220ms -> 600ms, p99 from 1.1s -> 2.4s on streaming endpoints. Error rates fairly flat, 5xx slight bump (0.02% -> 0.12%). Streaming stalls visible as long tails on KV-cache hit rates.

infra_sam: infra metrics show GPU node gpu-node-17 having repeated ECC correctable errors and thermal spikes. Node shows fan speed oscillation and occasional PCIe reset events.

infra_sam: posting quick dump from node:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
GPU 3
  Temperature
    GPU Current Temp : 92 C
  ECC Errors
    Volatile: 124 correctable, 3 uncorrectable
  Power Readings
    Power Draw : 320 W
```

infra_sam: also dmesg tail shows repeated pcie reset messages for gpu3 and driver spam about ECC corrected.

oncall_alex: ok plan: 1) enable immediate routing fallback to replica pool (lower-cost quantized variant) 2) cordon/drain gpu-node-17 from serving 3) spin up replacement capacity in us-west-2 4) monitor p95/p99 and customer error rates.

deployer_bot: running: `kubectl drain node/gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

deplyer_bot: drain started (pod eviction in progress) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ml_ops_jess: enabling fallback in routing rules now — switching 30% of streaming traffic to model-quant-q4_0 as canary that runs on GPU pool-b. Doing gradual shift.

incident_bot: Update: routing fallback applied. Canary shift at 30%. Continued p99 degradation? monitoring.

oncall_alex: customers impacted? any in-flight sessions dropped?

customer_success_raj: enterprise-acct-01 says a few long streaming sessions timed out; they're retrying. Will follow up after we confirm stability.

infra_sam: drain completed. Node marked unschedulable. Evacuated 12 pods. Starting hardware quarantine and reboot + firmware probe.

ml_ops_jess: initial metrics after fallback: p95 now ~280ms, p99 moving down to ~420ms. Streaming stall traces indicate KV-cache misses increased when requests spilled to different node groups.

oncall_alex: good. keep the canary at 30% for 10 minutes then ramp if stable. Also enable prefix-KV cache warm-up on new pool to reduce cold miss penalty.

ml_ops_jess: enabled cache warm-up script. snippet:
```
for key in $(cat hot_keys.txt); do curl -X POST https://cache-prewarm/prime -d "$key"; done
```

incident_bot: Paging note — severity: sev2 -> customer-visible latency, no system-wide outage. Notifying SRE rotation.

duty_lead_maya: assign follow-ups: infra_sam to run hardware repro, open ticket with vendor for GPU 3. ml_ops_jess to run regression test vs quantized fallback for generation quality. oncall_alex to coordinate postmortem.

infra_sam: vendor ticket opened: TCK-98421. attaching ECC logs and dmesg. Next steps: firmware update and burn-in tests on spare host.

ml_ops_jess: quick note on quality: quantized fallback increases token-level hallucination risk slightly for a tiny fraction of requests; will run targeted evals on the affected prompts. No major regressions observed in quick check.

oncall_alex: after 12 minutes of canary, p99 stable ~380ms, 5xx back to baseline. I'm going to ramp fallback from 30% -> 70% then 100% in 5m if metrics hold.

incident_bot: update: canary ramp to 70% done. p95 240ms, p99 360ms.

customer_success_raj: enterprise-acct-01 confirms improvements, timeouts stopped for new sessions. They asked for an incident update for their legal/compliance inbox.

oncall_alex: creating brief incident summary for customers and execs. Will schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PST.

ml_ops_jess: created perf dashboard snapshot and exported logs to s3://redwood-incidents/9698765432/metrics.tar.gz

infra_sam: hardware repro suggests intermittent ECC flares under sustained load — likely a marginal GPU module. We're recommending RMA for the accelerator and replacing the node.

duty_lead_maya: severity review: sev2, but potential repeat risk if other cards wear. Action item: run ECC sweep across fleet and add templated alert for ECC-corrected-rate > 50/min.

oncall_alex: agreed. also adding routing rule change to fall back earlier if p99 > 800ms for more than 2 minutes.

incident_bot: Incident timeline record created: 9698765432. Postmortem owners: ml_ops_jess, infra_sam, oncall_alex. Customer comm owner: customer_success_raj.

oncall_alex: closing live incident channel in 30m if metrics stable. Thanks everyone for fast coordination. :white_check_mark: 

customer_success_raj: I'll send the customer-facing summary and include mitigation steps and ETA for hardware RMA.

infra_sam: leaving node in quarantine and replacing tomorrow morning. Will follow up in postmortem with logs and firmware recommendations.

ml_ops_jess: follow-ups tracked in TICKET-INC-9698765432. will add eval artifacts.

incident_bot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring.

oncall_alex: final note — learned: need faster autoscaling for streaming pool and more aggressive pre-warming of KV cache on pool failovers. Add to postmortem action list.

oncall_alex: signing off, handing to SRE day team.
